newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany names suspects charged in disco bomb case.
newsitem.headline: Germany names suspects charged in disco bomb case.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Friday they had charged three Germans, one Palestinian and a Libyan in connection with a 1986 West Berlin nightclub bomb attack which provoked a U.S. air strike on Libya.
The charges against the five include murder and aiding and abetting the attack, in which two U.S. soldiers and a Turkish woman were killed and scores of off-duty U.S. military personnel were wounded.
State prosecutor Dieter Neumann told a news conference the three Germans charged were Verena Chanaa, her former husband Ali Chanaa and her sister Andrea Haeussler.
They also charged a former member of the Libyan secret service Musbah Eter and a Palestinian Yasser Shraydi, both workers at the Libyan embassy in East Berlin at the time.
Shraydi along with Verena and Ali Chanaa were charged with murder in three cases and setting off the explosion. The others were charged with aiding and abetting the crime.
Washington blamed Libya for the blast, in Berlin's Schoeneberg district, and bombed the Arab state, killing at least 15 people and wounding more than 100.
